class.name: NNPointGrid3DSearchSpace
class.brief_description: Search space that generates a grid of 3D sample points around a node.
class.description: Generates a lattice of [Node3D] candidate positions centered on [member point_grid_parent_node] (a flat XZ layer when [code]grid_size.y == 0[/code], or a 3D volume), optionally snapped to the 3D navigation mesh ([member use_navigation_mesh_positions]). Use this for tactical positioning queries in 3D (such as finding cover, flanking positions, or safe spots) when no hand-placed marker nodes exist. Choose a layout preset with [member point_grid_lattice_type] or customize density with [member grid_size], [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector], and [member point_grid_lattice_vector]. Keep spacing reasonable to avoid generating too many points. To visualize points while debugging, add a direct [Node3D] child named [code]DEBUG[/code] (for example, a [MeshInstance3D]); it will be duplicated for each generated point instead of plain [Node3D]s.

members.member: Width, height, and depth of the generated grid, centered on [member point_grid_parent_node]. A height of [code]0[/code] generates a single horizontal layer.
[NavigationServer3D] map [RID] used when [member use_navigation_mesh_positions] is enabled. Defaults to the viewport's 3D navigation map.
Local offset applied to all generated points before navigation snapping.
Generated [Node3D] candidate points parented under [member point_grid_parent_node].
Step size between consecutive base points along X, Y, and Z. Smaller values increase density. Must be positive.

Preset lattice pattern ([code]Square[/code], [code]Triangular[/code], [code]CenteredRectangular[/code], [code]Rectangular[/code], or [code]Custom[/code]). Choosing a preset updates [member point_grid_base_spacing_vector] and [member point_grid_lattice_vector].
Local offset from each base point to its paired lattice point (for creating square, staggered, or triangular grids).
[Node3D] that owns and centers the generated point grid (usually the AI actor).
If [code]true[/code], snaps each candidate point onto the closest point on the 3D navigation mesh before scoring.
